ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Gilda Radner

code.originalText: End of chemotherapy: CT and CA-125 response, and the start of olaparib maintenance

text.paragraph: End of chemotherapy: CT and CA-125 results, and the maintenance decision. [S]

Ms. Radner returns three weeks after her sixth and last cycle, all given on schedule. The CT a week ago shows no evidence of disease. Her energy is coming back, she walks most days, and her appetite is good. The tingling in her toes and fingertips is a little less than at cycle 4 and does not affect her hands or balance. Hot flashes continue at night. She saw Dr. Varghese with the CT result, and together they reviewed maintenance with olaparib, which she wants to start. She has no fever, cough, breathlessness, or bleeding. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 56.8 kg; blood pressure 114/72, pulse 76
Soft, non-tender; no fluid or mass
Pinprick slightly reduced over the toes only; vibration and reflexes normal; steady gait

Persistent bloating with tightness of her clothes, feeling full after a few bites, a dull lower abdominal and pelvic ache, and passing urine more often, on most days for about four weeks, in a woman of 39: the ovarian cancer symptom index is positive. Examination: a distended abdomen with shifting dullness and a firm, fixed, irregular mass in the right adnexa. Suspected ovarian cancer; transvaginal ultrasound, CT, CA-125 and gynecologic oncology review booked within the week
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abdominal symptoms; superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

High-grade serous carcinoma of both ovaries (Mullerian origin), diagnosed by image-guided omental core biopsy (PAX8 and WT1 positive, p53 aberrant), with bilateral adnexal masses, ascites, omental and diaphragmatic disease on CT: clinical FIGO stage IIIC; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented ovarian cancer
S — Synthetic histology and stage; the documented diagnosis was stage IV ovarian cancer (D).
Peritoneal and omental metastases of the ovarian cancer, with ascites
S — Synthetic extent of disease on CT and biopsy.
Family history of ovarian cancer in three relatives (her grandmother, an aunt, and a cousin) in a woman of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry; no genetic testing in the family is known
S — Synthetic coding of her documented family history; the basis for genetic counseling.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection on day 8 of the second chemotherapy cycle: two days of sore throat, runny nose and a dry cough, without fever; rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests negative; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Symptomatic surgical menopause after bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy at 39: hot flashes and night sweats
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic operation.
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy from paclitaxel: tingling in the toes and fingertips, grade 1 (sensory only, no effect on daily activities)
S — Synthetic common effect of paclitaxel.

list.item:
High-grade serous ovarian cancer, stage IIIC, complete response after surgery and chemotherapy (C56.3). Complete clinical response: no evidence of disease on CT and CA-125 9 U/mL. With a tumor BRCA1 pathogenic variant, olaparib maintenance for two years lowers the risk of recurrence substantially, as Dr. Varghese advised. Baseline blood count before olaparib: hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, neutrophils 2.6, platelets 214; creatinine 0.69 mg/dL. No interacting medicines; no grapefruit. She can no longer become pregnant. [S]
Olaparib 300 mg twice daily with food, starting today, for two years.
Blood count monthly for the first year, the first in four weeks at the preventive visit.
Report breathlessness, new cough, fever, bruising, or marked tiredness.
Surveillance with gynecologic oncology every three months for two years, with examination and CA-125; imaging only for symptoms or a rising CA-125.

Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Improving after the last paclitaxel. [S]
Review at each visit.

Symptomatic surgical menopause (E89.41). Hot flashes at night. Menopausal hormone therapy was discussed: it may be considered after high-grade serous ovarian cancer and would also protect her bones; she would rather wait and see how she feels on olaparib. [S]
Revisit at the next visit.
Bone density scan to be ordered at the preventive visit.

Follow-up: Preventive visit in four weeks with the first monthly blood count. Gynecologic oncology surveillance every three months. Call for breathlessness, new cough, fever, bruising, or the return of bloating or early fullness. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-13: periodic adult preventive visit after ovarian cancer treatment. [S]
